How to read this
  • Spread shows repeatability across recordings, not accuracy. A tool can repeat well and still be biased.
  • 448.50 ± 0.48 (10): median ± sd across the 10 recordings that tool solved. With 3 or 4 recordings the sd itself is rough.
  • (3/15): this tool has 3 of the family's 15 recordings.
  • fixed: Kalibr doesn't estimate this value. Its camera + IMU runs take intrinsics and baselines as input, from an MVIS export or, on T6 and T11, from its own camera-only calibration; T7 ELP-L readout is held at 0. The spread here isn't repeatability.
  • shown: the tool uses a different model here, so the value has no difference next to it.
  • other model: Kalibr's coefficients here belong to a different lens model.
  • not in model, not reported, no run, no data, no RS model, not in one run: the tool has no value for this row, and the words say why. no run means the tool never ran with this sensor; not in one run means it ran with each sensor, but no single run holds both ends of the baseline. not run, in the recordings line: the tool has no run for the family.
  • Differences: the column header gives the subtraction, using stored medians. No tool is the reference.
  • ◆: the difference is larger than the larger of the two sds. It marks disagreement, not an error in either tool.
  • ≠n: the two medians come from different numbers of recordings.
  • ≠ model: the tools' models differ, so no difference is shown. fit: reprojection error measures fit and isn't comparable across models.
  • ‡ td: MVIS splits the IMU into gyro (td) and accel (td + t_ga); Kalibr and Basalt have one timeline. Basalt − Kalibr is the like-for-like check.
  • Each family folds; the first is open. Click a family's title to open or close it.

MVIS 15 of 15 · Kalibr 15 of 15 on ELP-L, 13 of 15 on ELP-R · Basalt 15 of 15, shown only

Camera · bags 01–15 · Kalibr pinhole-radtan-rs, one camera per run

Read first: Lens models differ, so only readout has a difference, and Kalibr wasn't re-run after the ELP stamp correction. Basalt is shown only.

Notes

Like for like: Kalibr has 13 of 15 recordings on ELP-R. MVIS uses an equidistant lens model, Kalibr and Basalt radtan, so fx, fy, cx, cy and distortion have no difference, and the dist[2] and dist[3] rows hold different coefficients per tool. Basalt solves this rolling-shutter pair as global shutter. Kalibr wasn't re-run after the ELP stamp correction; we expect it to be unchanged, but that wasn't tested. MVIS estimates the board shape; Kalibr assumes a flat board.

Note: Kalibr's rolling-shutter model calibrates one camera at a time, so it has no ELP stereo baseline. ELP-R bags 8 and 13 failed (autodiff overflow at bag-freq 15; the bag-freq-10 retry overflowed again on bag 8 and converged to a non-physical basin on bag 13) and are excluded.

Basalt: Basalt has no rolling-shutter model: it solves the ELP pair as global shutter with pinhole-radtan8 (seeded from kb4), so its T2 values are shown only. Since 2026-11-01 MVIS solves the ELP with the equidistant model while the Kalibr RS runs are radtan: readout is compared; fx, fy, cx, cy and distortion are shown without a difference because the lens models differ.

MVIS 15 of 15 · Kalibr 14 of 15 · Basalt not run

Camera + IMU · bags 01–15 · Kalibr with ELP-L as global shutter (bag 8 excluded)

Read first: Kalibr treats ELP-L as global shutter; its intrinsics and baselines are inputs from an MVIS export. Data settings differ: see Notes.

Notes, including why Basalt has no run

Basalt not run: Basalt cannot calibrate T7 — no rolling-shutter model for ELP-L, one IMU per run, and one time offset shared by all cameras (the t265 and ELP clocks share no frame stamps).

Like for like: Kalibr has 14 of 15 recordings (bag 8 failed). Its ELP-L readout is fixed at 0, and ELP-L's stamps were shifted by the MVIS td of the same bag before each Kalibr run. Its td and lever are solved given these inputs. MVIS uses two corners per tag, non-base cameras at 4 Hz or lower and an estimated board shape; Kalibr has none of these.

Note: MVIS solves t265 fisheye 1 (GS) + ELP-L (rolling shutter, readout estimated) + both IMUs. Kalibr's camera + IMU solver is global-shutter only, so its runs take ELP-L as a GS camera and its readout tr is reported as 0 (its global-shutter model, not an estimate). Kalibr bag 8 is excluded: its base gyro scales (1.23 / 2.23) are far from the other 14 bags (about 1.01), a failed solve; MVIS keeps bag 8, so its n is 15 and Kalibr's is 14.

Bag: topics copied with the ELP stamps shifted by the MVIS td of the same bag (retime_bag.py). Cameras /t265/fisheye1/image_raw, /elp/split_sync_image_node/left/image_raw · IMUs /t265/imu (200 Hz), /imu/data (400 Hz) (imu0 = Kalibr's reference IMU).

Kalibr's camera + IMU solver has no rolling-shutter model: ELP-L enters as a global-shutter camera (its line_delay dropped from the chain) and its stamps are pre-shifted by the MVIS td of the same bag (retime_bag.py; Kalibr's correlation init otherwise lands 100–200 ms off). The reported td = applied shift + Kalibr's residual.

camchain.yaml: the MVIS kalibr-variant export of the same recording (cam_imu_camchain-imucam.yaml): intrinsics held fixed, T_cam_imu as the initial value, topics set to the bag's. IMU noise = the MVIS regression defaults (core/config.py), so both tools weight the IMU alike.
